set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 full-codebase review.

Problem:
managed/ManagedController.scala guarded invokeSubmission with guaranteeCase,
recovering the submission claim on Outcome.Errored and Outcome.Canceled. But the
operation returns F[Either[ControlFailure, ManagedAttempt]], and a returned Left is
Outcome.Succeeded, so a typed rejection of RecordSubmission skipped recovery
entirely. sbatch had already run and the attempt stayed in Submitting with no
recovery event -- a job exists on the cluster and nothing in the journal names it.

This is a false-certainty bug of the class Phase A targets, and it is invisible to
the suite by construction: the store stub always accepted, so the branch was never
taken. Demonstrated by injecting a store that rejects RecordSubmission:
"expected AcceptanceUnknown, found Submitting".

invokeCancellation carried the identical shape, where a rejected RecordCancellation
would strand an attempt in Cancelling after scancel may already have run.

Acceptance:
- Both paths recover on a typed rejection as well as on a raised failure or
  cancellation.
- Recovery stays inside the caller's uncancelable region, and the guarantee has
  already completed when the branch runs, so no path recovers twice.
- Test demonstrated RED against the parent commit.
set.title: P8.A9: Recover a claim when the record is rejected, not only when it raises
